**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** — at the next minor cut, since this is a `feat` (per AGENTS.md, a feat merges at the cut, not on review).

## What looks good

- The fallback runs only when no candidate passes the plain gate, so every part that already fitted keeps a bit-for-bit identical fit — the design makes the "no golden changes" claim checkable, and the touched suites agree.
- The direction is held while the kept set settles; the decision file records the #208 regression that motivated that (a refined direction swinging onto a prism's pencil). The halving cut (annealing-style) with the MIN_KEPT / MIN_KEPT_SHARE backstops is a sound, deterministic IRLS-with-consensus construction, provenance lines present on both new files.
- Degenerate paths refuse cleanly: non-finite answering area, `line()` solve failure, and a settled set below the backstops all return `None` → the existing refusal; rounds are bounded (no hang). No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests in the new code.
- `CONSENSUS_SHARE`, the held direction, the halving cut, the 0.75 choice, and the known meridian-block limit are all recorded in `docs/decisions/113-lathe-axis-fit.md` in the right format; refusal text is now unit-tested; the PR body carries a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #113`; commit subject is conventional; no `CHANGELOG.md` edit.
- The pinning tests are the right shape: fit-level (motion) and law-level (app), including the negative fixtures (30 % lump, box) refused *by name*.

## Local results (PR head trial-merged with current main)

Trial merge with `origin/main` (a6e9c7c) merged cleanly (only `spindle_law.rs` auto-merged, against main's `wcs_context` signature fix — no semantic clash). Windows 11, debug, own worktree.

| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| build `cargo test -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --no-run` | ok |
| `camcraft-motion` lib | 153 passed / 0 failed (incl. the 4 new `axis_consensus` tests) |
| `camcraft-app` lib | 95 passed / 0 failed (incl. the 3 new `spindle_law` tests) |
| app `lathe_spindle_keyed` | 6 passed / 0 failed |
| app `lathe_spindle_fit` | 3 passed / 0 failed |
| app `lathe_spindle_law` | 8 passed / 0 failed |
| app `drilling_cross_spindle` | 7 passed / 0 failed |
| app `rotary_fixtures` / `rotary_verify` | 4 / 9 passed, 0 failed |
| motion `rotary` (axis fit, gate map) | 10 passed / 0 failed |
| motion `turning_prof` | 8 passed / 0 failed |
| motion `swarf_pose_continuity` | 5 passed / 0 failed — the 2 failures you saw on macOS pass here; main-side nothing touched swarf/stamp since your base, so this reads as platform-specific, not a defect |
| clippy `-p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean (no warnings) |

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. **Scope of the loosened gate.** `axis_consensus::fit` hangs off `fit_report`, so it opens the consensus axis to *every* consumer of `axis::fit` — 4-axis rotary (`rotary.rs`, `rotary_bar.rs`, `rotary_offset.rs`), the axial and cross drills — not only the lathe. A part with 24 % of its surface set aside was refused by those ops before and will now generate. The spindle law's silhouette/note story covers the lathe; do the rotary kinds have an equivalent "set aside, named" story, or was gating the fallback to the turning path (#113's ask) considered? Genuine question — the suites pass and the 4-axis offsets are read off the real surface — I just don't know where the 5-axis/rotary boundary was drawn in your testing.
2. `axis.rs` is 411 lines, just over the ~400 guideline — you flagged it yourself; a future split along the `refusal`/`judge` seam would settle it.
3. Minor: in `axis_consensus::consensus`, a `line()` failure on a kept set (`let moved = line(...)?`) declines that whole direction even though the line already held at the current `ax` — conservative and safe, but one round's solve hiccup discards an otherwise-settled candidate. Fine as is; noting for the next reader.
4. The `Fit { plain, ..f }` override (reporting the true least-squares line while `reweigh` was seeded with the consensus line) is only consumed by tests today — worth a sentence in the decision file so nobody later reads `plain` as "what reweigh started from."

## Process

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand. This is a `feat`, so per AGENTS.md it waits for the next minor cut rather than merging straight away.
